discovery: Discovery of conductance quantization in ballistic quantum point contacts
subfield: Mesoscopic physics / quantum transport in nanostructures
motivation: In 1988 two teams, in Delft/Eindhoven (van Wees, van Houten and co-workers) and in Cambridge (Wharam, Pepper and co-workers), independently found that the conductance of a narrow constriction in a two-dimensional electron gas is quantized in steps of 2e^2/h, without any magnetic field. This was direct, striking proof that electrical conduction through a nanoscale conductor is governed by transmission of individual quantum modes, as in the Landauer-Buttiker picture. The quantum point contact became the founding experiment and basic tool of mesoscopic physics. It is used as a sensitive charge detector for spin and charge qubits in quantum dots, it underlies electron quantum optics and shot-noise studies, and it is the conceptual basis for ballistic hybrid superconducting devices, Andreev spectroscopy and topological-qubit readout. Few discoveries have turned a quantum-mechanical subtlety into such a universal and controllable device.
